stateKeys.name: snoozeCount
stateKeys.type: integer 0..2, how many times the user snoozed an overdue item

stateKeys.name: dueAt
stateKeys.type: string, ISO-8601 due timestamp ('' when no due date is set)

stateKeys.name: doneVia
stateKeys.type: string, how the item ended: 'completed' or a drop reason ('' until terminal)

dataFields.dueAt: string - the due timestamp this (timer) event was scheduled for; must match the item's current dueAt or the event is stale

dataFields.until: string - ISO-8601 new due timestamp, non-empty; recorded verbatim as the new dueAt

dataFields.reason: string - why the item was dropped, non-empty

specialRules.name: corrections-are-event-driven
specialRules.note: The ONLY backward edge in the lifecycle is overdue -> open, taken ONLY by SNOOZE, which records the new due date (data.until) verbatim in dueAt and increments snoozeCount by exactly 1. No action exists that re-opens or re-schedules an item without a concrete signal.

specialRules.name: bounded-snooze-budget-triages
specialRules.note: SNOOZE with snoozeCount already at 2 moves the item to needsTriage (a human decides: COMPLETE or DROP) instead of granting another lap. needsTriage accepts only COMPLETE and DROP.

specialRules.name: stale-due-timer-reject
specialRules.note: DUE_PASSED applies only in 'open' AND only when data.dueAt equals the item's current dueAt. A timer for a superseded due date, or firing after the item completed/was dropped, is an observable rejection (post == pre), never a fault — this is what makes durable at-least-once timers safe with zero cancellation races.
specialRules.whenState: any state where todoState != 'open' or data.dueAt != dueAt

specialRules.name: reopen-is-a-new-instance
specialRules.note: completed and archived are frozen terminals: there is deliberately no REOPEN action. Un-completing a todo is creating a new instance (fresh budget, fresh journal), not mutating a settled one.

noOpRule: An action that does not apply in the current state is reject(reason) — an observable no-op with post == pre.
